now.title: 3.7.0: RT Markdown Reader, on this computer
now.note: Released. Tested both ways against the real RT Markdown Reader.

items.title: Link the two apps
items.text: Turn on Linked apps in Preferences in both, then link them once. Send a document across each way.

items.title: Still to come on its side
items.text: RT Markdown Reader sends only to a linked app so far, and doesn’t read pictures yet.

items.title: Still open from earlier
items.text: Your own test of the lock and of Find my files, a real Word manuscript, Pages on a Mac, and a real Scrivener project.

waiting.title: A test and {decisions} decisions
waiting.text: A power cut during a lock is simulated, not tested for real, and the decisions below. None of them hold up 3.7.

questions.q: Can the apps detect each other when they’re installed?
questions.a: Not yet: today they find each other only while running. v3.8, the next release, adds an installed list and an Apps panel in every app, to the suite’s shared rules.

questions.q: What happens to pictures in an imported file?
questions.a: From v3.5 they stay with the book as attachments, encrypted like the rest of the project. They sit beside the writing and don’t appear on the page yet.

questions.q: Why did StoryTracker move off WPF?
questions.a: WPF only runs on Windows. The new app is Electron and JavaScript, like RT Markdown Reader, so one app runs on Windows, Mac and Linux. The old C# code is kept in legacy-wpf.

questions.q: Does it use the same themes as RT Markdown Reader?
questions.a: The same set, as copies. It has all of RT Markdown Reader's themes, the old app's Plum, Evergreen, Blue/Orange and Aero, and a new one, Slate, plus Glass with any theme but High Contrast. A theme added to one app doesn't reach the other by itself. Packs, under Later, would change that.
Yes, in v3.19, using RT Markdown Reader's offline voices, with the dictionary's pronunciations. You can already send a chapter to RT Markdown Reader and have it read there.

questions.q: Will the dictionary know how to say words?
questions.a: Yes. In v3.12 each word can carry a pronunciation guide, for invented words and words from other languages. Read aloud uses it, and so do RT Markdown Reader's voices through App Link, so a name is taught once.

questions.q: Can more themes and fonts be downloaded?
questions.a: Theme and font packs are under Later.

questions.q: Were these features taken from RT Markdown Reader?
questions.a: Partly. Most came from what you said you need. In November the two roadmaps were compared feature by feature, and what this app was missing was added: v3.8, v3.18 to v3.20, and wider v3.12 and v3.14.

questions.q: How do I hand an AI a chapter as Markdown?
questions.a: Markdown export arrives in v3.3, App Link sends a chapter to RT Markdown Reader in v3.7 (both apps have to be up to date), and Claude can work with the book directly in v3.14.

questions.q: Can it be tested on real stories?
questions.a: Yes, once the basics work. Your stories and Notion become the test bed, and what you need for how you write goes on this roadmap.

questions.q: Will it make EPUBs that KDP accepts?
questions.a: It makes EPUBs that pass EPUBCheck, the official validator, with no errors or warnings. The test that counts is uploading one to KDP’s previewer, which is yours to do.
